description: We are Team ABF, a small team from Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Bunyod is the designer and coder, and Faruch is the speaker who presents our work. We also use Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, to help us write code from our instructions. We care about using space data to solve real problems for ordinary people, and our project, ABF Field Shift, is a free web app that helps small farmers see drought, heat, fire and disease risks for their own field using NASA data.
summary:
ABF Field Shift is a free web app designed to help small farmers decide what to plant and when. A farmer draws their field on a 3D terrain map. The app then shows the field’s elevation, slope and slope direction. It also shows the climate risks for that place: drought, heat, wildfire and crop disease.

The risks come from NASA data. We use 20 years of NASA POWER climate records and NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections. From these the app recommends three crops, a three-year crop rotation, how much water the crops need each year and where the nearest water source is.

It solves the problem by turning NASA Earth observation data into simple advice that a farmer can use without any expert training. It is available in English, Russian and Tajik. It also includes accessibility features and a Lite mode for internet connections. Farmers can use it as a guest or with a private account.

It matters because farmers in drought- and heat-prone regions like Tajikistan are the most exposed to climate change. They often do not have access, to this kind of data. ABF Field Shift gives them the information they need to make decisions.
details:
What it does and how it works. The farmer opens ABF Field Shift and draws their field on a 3D terrain map. The app checks that the shape is on farmland and not on a city or water. It then measures the field’s area, elevation, slope steepness and slope direction. Next it pulls NASA data for that exact place using 20 years of NASA POWER climate records and NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections. From these it calculates drought, heat, wildfire and crop disease risk. It then recommends 3 suitable crops, a 3 year crop rotation, the yearly water need, and the nearest water source. The panel is in English, Russian and Tajik.

Benefits. Farmers get advice for their own field instead of a general regional forecast. The app is free and needs no expert knowledge. Guest mode works with no sign-in, and there is an optional private account with a username and password, with no email needed. A Lite mode and accessibility features help people with slow connections or disabilities.

Intended impact. We want to help small farmers in drought- and heat-prone regions, such as Tajikistan, choose crops that fit a changing climate. This should reduce crop losses, wasted water and fire damage.

Tools and technology. The backend is built with Node.js and Express. It keeps the API keys secret on the server and adds rate limits and caching. The frontend is plain HTML and JavaScript. It uses MapLibre GL JS for the 3D terrain, Terra Draw for drawing fields, Turf.js for geometry and Chart.js for charts. The data comes from NASA POWER, NASA FIRMS, Terrarium elevation data and OpenStreetMap for land checks, plus IPstack and Weatherstack for location and weather. The app is hosted on Render with an uptime monitor, and the code is public on GitHub, https://github.com/buned2023-pixel/abf-field-shift. We used Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, to help write the code from our instructions. We designed the product and directed every step.

Creativity. The main idea is a 3D terrain view where the farmer draws a real field and instantly sees the slope, the climate risks and the crop plan for that spot. We also designed our own logo, and we added Tajik, a language that few tools support.

Factors we considered. We thought about data accuracy, keeping API keys private, API quotas, accessibility, slow internet, user privacy, and a free public link that needs no password or registration. This is an advisory tool and not an official NASA product.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) – daily climate data.
NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) – active fire detections from MODIS and VIIRS.
projectRefs: OpenStreetMap (map data, used for the land and water check)
